content:
Alex (Recruiter): candidate Diego Ramos (Backend Eng) has a competing offer. He's asking for a T2->T3 uplift, an earlier start (one week sooner), and confirmation on benefits eligibility day-1 because of healthcare coverage gap. Current offer: base $120,000 + $10k sign-on + standard RS. Can we close today? cc @Jordan

Jordan (Hiring Manager): Diego's microservices work is critical for the release. I can move some hiring ops budget. Manager asks for provisional uplift if that helps expedite.

Aisha (People Ops): Two things to coordinate: 1) provisional band uplift (policy allows up to +7% base without committee with documentation), and 2) benefits enrollment timing — benefits normally start first of month after 30 days; can we make an exception for day-1 medical eligibility? That needs Payroll and Benefits sign-off.

Priya (Comp & Benefits): We can approve a provisional uplift of +6% base (no committee) if manager justification is posted and candidate signs a 6-month review clause. For benefits, standard policy is not day-1, but we can advance medical coverage start to day 1 if Payroll confirms funding for retroactives; otherwise we can offer a one-time health stipend to cover gap.

Lina (Payroll): Payroll quick-check: to make benefits active day-1 we need to process a retroactive premium payment and enroll the new hire immediately; finance must approve one-time retro payment (~$650 for medical in this plan). Alternatively a $700 health stipend paid on day 1 is simpler. Which do you prefer?

Jordan (Hiring Manager): Manager justification: Diego's departure would require reassigning 3 sprints of work and risk slippage on the release. Provisional uplift avoids losing momentum. I prefer the stipend approach to avoid retro payroll work.

Priya (Comp & Benefits): approve provisional uplift: +6% base ($127,200), sign-on unchanged. Health stipend $700 on day 1 approved. Candidate must accept provisional review clause and stipend acknowledgement.

Sam (Legal): I'll add clause language: "Provisional Compensation Adjustment subject to 6-month review; health stipend is a one-time payment and not part of base pay; benefits enrollment remains subject to plan rules." Need recruiter to include exact wording in offer.

Alex (Recruiter): Sending revised offer with +6% provisional uplift, 6-month review clause, and $700 health stipend on day 1. Candidate said day-1 coverage is a deciding factor. I'll post acceptance when signed.

Aisha (People Ops): I'll log this as a provisional comp exception and create a 6-month follow-up in our tracker. If anything changes loop this thread.
